approved: Housing Australia Amendment (Transparency and Reporting) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would require Housing Australia to report quarterly on its spending, projects, and operations.
Housing Australia must give the Minister a quarterly report covering expenditure, program data, guarantees, and board minutes.
The first report is due after the first full quarter following the bill's commencement, and the Minister must table it in Parliament within 7 sitting days.
Requires Housing Australia to prepare and provide quarterly reports to the Minister.
Specifies the information each quarterly report must include, such as spending, project numbers, guarantee breakdowns by income decile, and summarised board minutes.
Prevents the Minister from directing Housing Australia on its quarterly reporting function.
Housing Australia, the Minister, and Parliament.

Introduced the Housing Australia Amendment (Transparency and Reporting) Bill 2026, arguing Housing Australia lacks accountability after the Australian National Audit Office found the Housing Australia Future Fund delivered only 1,432 homes, nearly half of them purchased rather than built, against a target of 40,000, and proposed mandatory quarterly reports on spending, guarantees and board minutes free from ministerial direction.
